text:
Aisha Patel: Quick question — I'm putting together the latency page for the customer deck. Where do folks usually pull TTFT / p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec by model? Need dashboard links + example queries I can paste, and any recommended alert thresholds.

Samir Gupta: For dashboards: Grafana -> 'Inference / Latency' has model dropdown. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/inf-latency/Inference-Latency?orgId=1 . Use the model var at top.

Samir Gupta: Example PromQL for TTFT p95 (adjust the metric name if needed):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
```
That gives per-model p95 request duration (TTFT if you filter by label `phase="first_token"` or use a TTFT-specific metric). If we have a metric `redwood_inference_ttft_seconds` then: 
```
quantile_over_time(0.95, redwood_inference_ttft_seconds[5m])
```

Samir Gupta: Tokens/sec (per-model):
```
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_generated_total[1m])) by (model)
```
Or if we expose tokens_per_sec: `avg_over_time(tokens_per_sec[1m]) by (model)`

Lucy Chen: For traces, use Tempo/Jaeger: https://tempo.redwood.ai/search -> set service=`inference` and tag `model:<model-name>` then look at tail traces around p99. That's good to root-cause TTFT spikes (cold KV, kernel fallback, slow IO).

Lucy Chen: Logs (Loki): https://loki.redwood.ai/ Explore with `{app=\"inference\", model=\"<model-name>\"} |= \"first_token\"` to see request-level logs.

Kevin Li: Alert tuning: rules live in infra-alerts repo: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/alerting/-/blob/main/ttft-rules.yaml . Current suggested thresholds (starter):
- hosted/api: p95 TTFT > 250ms for 5m -> pager
- dedicated: p95 TTFT > 500ms for 5m -> page (higher tolerance for some dedicated configs)
- p99 TTFT > 1s -> page
- tokens/sec drop: >30% drop vs 15m baseline -> page
These are our defaults but tweak per-customer SLA.

Maria Gomez: Also include `tokens/sec per instance` grafana panel (variable: instance) — helps differentiate capacity vs latency. If tokens/sec is low but TTFT high, probably cold cache or backend stall.

Aisha Patel: Nice — do we have a short example query I can paste into the deck to show p95 TTFT for a specific model?

Samir Gupta: Yup — paste this (replace <model>):
```
# p95 TTFT for `mistral-7b` over last 1h
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) and on (model) group_left() (model==\"mistral-7b\")
```
(If using a TTFT-specific gauge)
```
quantile_over_time(0.95, redwood_inference_ttft_seconds{model=\"mistral-7b\"}[1h])
```

Kevin Li: One pro tip: use the dashboard timepicker `Last 1h` and the model variable. For decks we screenshot the panel with `stat` + legend disabled.

Lucy Chen: For deep-dive traces, look for `kv_cache_miss=true` or `quantize=fallback` tags on spans — those correlate strongly with TTFT tails.

Aisha Patel: Perfect. Can someone add the Grafana panel link for `mistral-7b` so I can screenshot?

Samir Gupta: Added quick panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/inf-latency/Inference-Latency?var-model=mistral-7b&panelId=42 — should be viewable to the org.

Maria Gomez: FYI if you need to relax alerts for a customer during migration, ping me and I can add a temporary silence in Alertmanager.

Aisha Patel: Thanks all — I'll assemble the slides and tag you for review. :thumbsup:

eng-sre-bot: Note: alert rule change requests must include `reason`, `start_time`, `end_time`, and `owner` to be approved. See PR template: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/alerting/-/blob/main/README.md#silence-requests
